title: Fine-tune Llama 3.1 with LoRA using Soup CLI
description: How to fine-tune Meta Llama 3.1 8B with LoRA on a single GPU using Soup CLI. Full example: install, dataset, YAML config, training, and export.

blocks.html:
Fine-tune Llama 3.1 with LoRA using Soup CLI

This guide shows how to fine-tune Meta Llama 3.1 8B with LoRA adapters on a custom dataset using Soup CLI. End-to-end from install to inference on a single GPU; how long the training step takes depends on your dataset size, sequence length and card, and no timing is promised here.

Why LoRA on Llama 3.1?

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) trains only a small fraction (~0.1%) of model parameters, which means:

  • Train 8B parameter Llama 3.1 on a single 24GB GPU (RTX 4090, A10)
  • Checkpoints are tiny (~100MB instead of 16GB)
  • Faster training and easier experimentation

1. Install

Since v0.71.0 the base soup-cli package is a light, PyTorch-free CLI. [train] adds the training stack; [fast] adds Unsloth on top. Installing [fast] alone cannot train. Since v0.77.0 Soup needs Python 3.11 to 3.13 (>=3.11,<3.14); on Python 3.10, pip keeps installing v0.76.x.

The [fast] extra adds Unsloth for 2–5× training speedup on Llama-family models.

2. Prepare your dataset

Use the Alpaca format (JSON list of instruction/input/output triples):

Save as train.json. One row only shows the shape of the file. Soup holds out 10% of the rows for validation by default (data.val_split), and a one-row file leaves nothing to train on: since v0.76.0 soup train --dry-run on it exits 1 with No training rows: train.json loaded 0 train samples as format 'alpaca'. Use your real dataset.

3. Create the config

Save as llama31.yaml:

blocks.code:
base: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
task: sft
backend: unsloth            # root-level, NOT under training

data:
  train: train.json
  format: alpaca
  max_length: 2048          # sequence length lives under data

training:
  epochs: 3
  lr: 2.0e-4                # the key is lr, not learning_rate
  batch_size: 2
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
  gradient_checkpointing: true   # since v0.77.0 the default false turns Unsloth's off
  lora:
    r: 16                   # LoRA turns on when r > 0; there is no enabled flag
    alpha: 32
    dropout: 0.05
    target_modules: [q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj]

output: ./runs/llama31

blocks.html:
Spelling matters, and until v0.74.0 nothing told you so. Writing learning_rate instead of lr, or nesting backend under training, used to be dropped in silence and the default used instead. Since v0.74.0 loading a config walks the whole tree and reports every key it cannot place, and since v0.75.0 the config is refused: soup train exits 1 before the training stack is imported and prints unknown config key 'training.learning_rate' - refused. When the key is close to a real one the message adds a suggestion (bacth_size gets did you mean 'batch_size'?); learning_rate is not close to lr, so you get the refusal alone. Check the spelling against Configuration.

Why gradient_checkpointing: true is spelled out (v0.77.0, #1981). Through v0.76.x the Unsloth backend always used Unsloth's own checkpointing kernel, whatever the config said. Since v0.77.0 it honours training.gradient_checkpointing, and the schema default is false, which turns checkpointing off and uses more activation memory. true keeps Unsloth's kernel, as every earlier release used.

Before you train

Run soup doctor --config llama31.yaml first. Since v0.76.0 many more settings are refused when the config loads, each naming the field and what to change, so a config that loaded on an older release can stop loading. soup doctor --config prints the error and exits 2 without loading a model (it stops at the first cross-field refusal, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error), and since v0.77.0 it no longer prints All checks passed! above a refusal. Several things v0.76 only warned about are refused at v0.77.0, for example a staged field (validated, read by nothing) set away from its default, which stops the load with a line ending refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., and the deprecated data.remove_unused_columns: true. See Config refusals.

4. Train

In a script or CI job, pass --yes: since v0.77.0 soup train with its stdin piped or redirected and no --yes exits 3 instead of waiting at the confirmation prompt.

Soup detects your GPU and trains the LoRA adapters through Unsloth (backend: unsloth). FlashAttention is not switched on for you: training.use_flash_attn defaults to false. How long it takes depends on your sequence length, batch size and hardware; soup profile --config llama31.yaml estimates memory and speed before you start.

5. Chat with your fine-tuned model

blocks.code:
# Merge LoRA into base model and export GGUF for Ollama
soup export --model ./runs/llama31 --format gguf --quant q4_k_m

blocks.html:
Soup writes the training output (the adapter and tokenizer) straight into the output directory, so ./runs/llama31 above is the config's output: value, and there is no latest subdirectory. Without --output, the GGUF is written next to the model directory as ./runs/llama31.q4_k_m.gguf.

Troubleshooting

Out of memory? Enable QLoRA (a 4-bit base model). Note 4bit is already the default, so this is only worth setting explicitly if you changed it:

Slow training? Ensure backend: unsloth is set at the root of the config (not under training) and that you installed pip install "soup-cli[train,fast]".
